skill.name: meeting-insights-analyzer
skill.description: Analyzes meeting transcripts and recordings to uncover behavioral patterns, communication insights, and actionable feedback. Identifies when you avoid conflict, use filler words, dominate conversations, or miss opportunities to listen. Perfect for professionals seeking to improve their communication and leadership skills.
skill.summary: Reviews meeting transcripts to find communication patterns, examples, and improvement actions.
skill.author: ComposioHQ

content.value_statement: Meeting transcripts can hide repeated habits that affect trust, clarity, and leadership. This skill helps Claude, Codex, or Claude Code turn transcripts into specific feedback and next steps.
actual_capabilities: Finds recurring communication patterns across meeting transcripts.
Identifies conflict avoidance, interruptions, filler words, and listening signals.
Calculates speaking ratios, question patterns, and meeting participation trends.
Provides timestamped examples when transcripts include timestamps.
Compares meetings across folders or time periods for progress tracking.
Suggests practical next steps for communication and facilitation improvement.
limitations: Requires accessible transcripts or recordings that have already been transcribed.
Works best when files include speaker labels, dates, and timestamps.
Cannot verify tone, intent, or body language beyond the transcript content.
May need user confirmation to identify the correct speaker in ambiguous files.

use_cases.title: Improve leadership communication
use_cases.description: Review recurring behaviors in team meetings and receive examples that support focused improvement.

use_cases.title: Prepare performance review evidence
use_cases.description: Collect concrete meeting examples that show communication strengths, growth areas, and progress over time.

use_cases.title: Coach meeting facilitation
use_cases.description: Analyze how a speaker manages agenda flow, draws in quieter voices, and handles disagreement.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze one meeting
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner analysis of a single transcript.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this meeting transcript. Identify my main communication strengths, growth areas, and three specific examples from the meeting.

prompt_templates.title: Find conflict avoidance
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused review of a behavior pattern.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the transcripts in this folder. Find moments where I avoided direct feedback or difficult conversations, and suggest better phrasing.

prompt_templates.title: Compare meeting periods
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare my meetings from Q1 and Q2. Track listening signals, interruptions, questions asked, and speaking ratio changes.

prompt_templates.title: Create a development plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced synthesis for coaching or review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze all available transcripts. Build a communication development plan with patterns, evidence, risks, strengths, and weekly practice actions.

output_examples.input: Analyze my last five team meetings for facilitation style.
output: Summary of speaking ratio, question balance, agenda control, and inclusion patterns.
Examples of strong facilitation and missed opportunities with meeting names or timestamps.
Recommended changes for the next two team meetings.

output_examples.input: Tell me where I avoided conflict in these transcripts.
output: A list of indirect or hedged statements from the transcripts.
Short explanations of why each moment reduced clarity.
Alternative direct phrasing for each example.

output_examples.input: Compare my Q1 and Q2 listening habits.
output: A period comparison of interruptions, clarifying questions, and follow-up references.
Evidence of improvement or regression with representative examples.
A short action plan for the next review period.

best_practices: Use transcripts with consistent speaker names, dates, and timestamps.
Ask for one or two behaviors at a time when you need depth.
Review sensitive meeting data locally and remove private details when possible.
anti_patterns: Do not treat transcript analysis as a complete measure of intent or character.
Do not combine unrelated meetings without explaining the date range and context.
Do not publish examples from private meetings without consent.

faq.question: What files work best with this skill?
faq.answer: Plain text, Markdown, VTT, SRT, and exported transcript files work best when they include speaker labels.

faq.question: Can it analyze recordings directly?
faq.answer: The skill is designed around transcripts. Recordings should be transcribed before analysis.

faq.question: Does it need internet access?
faq.answer: No. The documented workflow uses local transcript files and does not require network access.

faq.question: Can it compare improvement over time?
faq.answer: Yes. It can compare transcript folders or date ranges when meetings are named or grouped clearly.

faq.question: Can it identify who speaks most?
faq.answer: Yes. It can estimate speaking ratios when transcripts include reliable speaker turns.

faq.question: How should sensitive transcripts be handled?
faq.answer: Keep files local, limit access, and redact private information before sharing outputs.
